data.description:
FOUND BY. Reviewing PR #417 (C11-204), which removed the app-modal runModal fallback from the browser insecure-HTTP prompt and the JS dialog paths.

CONTEXT. Before #417, 'c11 browser open http://...' behind a backgrounded window put up an app-modal alert nobody could see and wedged every surface in the app, for up to 6.8 hours in the measured worst case. #417 correctly replaced that with a safe default: with no window available to host the sheet, the insecure-HTTP navigation is denied without prompting.

THE GAP. That is strictly better than a hang, but it is silent from the caller's side. An agent that runs 'c11 browser open http://example.com' while the window is backgrounded now gets a navigation that simply does not happen. The only trace is an NSLog line in the app's stderr, which the calling agent cannot see. The agent has no way to distinguish 'the page failed to load' from 'c11 refused an insecure navigation because no human was available to approve it', and no way to consent to the navigation on its own authority.

This matters because socket-driven browser navigation is a routine c11 workflow: it is how agents validate web work (see the c11-browser skill), and doing it against a local http:// dev server behind an unfocused window is the common case, not the edge case.

WORK. Give the caller an actionable answer. Two pieces, either or both:
1. The socket command should return a structured error naming the reason, so the agent sees 'insecure HTTP navigation blocked: no window available to prompt' rather than a silent no-op.
2. Provide an explicit opt-in so an agent can consent without a human: a flag on the open verb, or a socket verb to add a host to the insecure-HTTP allowlist. Prefer scoping it narrowly (localhost and private-range hosts are the realistic need for dev-server validation).

Whatever the shape, the c11-browser skill must be updated to match, per the CLAUDE.md rule that a CLI or socket change is incomplete until the skill teaches it.

RELATION. Follow-up to C11-204 / PR #417. Not a blocker for that PR: the hang fix is worth landing on its own, and this is additive.
data.title: Socket-driven browser navigation fails silently when it cannot prompt

data.body:
# C11-207 complete — merged as 40c900194 (PR #431)

## What changed

Socket-driven browser navigation to a non-allowlisted plain-HTTP host is no longer silent.

**Navigation reports what it did.** `BrowserPanel.navigate(to:)` / `navigateSmart(_:)` /
`requestNavigation(_:intent:)` return a `BrowserNavigationDisposition` — `.proceeded`,
`.prompting(host:)`, `.blocked(host:reason:)` — also recorded on the panel as
`lastNavigationDisposition`, so a navigation that happens inside `BrowserPanel.init` is
readable after construction.

| Verb | Refused | Prompt pending |
|---|---|---|
| `browser.navigate` | `insecure_http_blocked` error naming host, url, reason, remedy | ok + `insecure_http: {status: "prompted", …}` |
| `browser.open_split` | ok + `insecure_http: {status: "blocked", …}` — the verb's promise (a surface exists) is kept, so the caller keeps refs to retry or clean up | ok + same fragment |
| `browser.url.get` | carries the same fragment; where an asynchronously refused navigation becomes legible | |

**The opt-in.** `--allow-insecure-http` on `browser open|open-split|new` and
`browser goto|navigate` (socket: `allow_insecure_http: true`) consents to one navigation to
one host, including that navigation's HTTP redirects to the same host. It grants nothing the
socket caller lacks (`browser.eval` already runs arbitrary JS), persists nothing, and leaves
the allowlist untouched. The CLI also surfaces a structured error's `hint` (error `data` is
otherwise dropped) and says on the text line when a prompt is pending or a navigation was
refused.

**Loopback decision: unchanged, deliberately.** `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`,
`*.localtest.me` were already default-allowed, so the ticket's named case needed documenting,
not changing. Private ranges were *not* added: they are readable on a shared network, and
widening the default for every human user to save agents one flag is the wrong trade.
Per-navigation consent covers tailnet hostnames and public HTTP that a host-range scope would
have left just as silent.

**Two pre-existing defects fixed in the same mechanism.** The one-time bypass was consumed by
the caller-side pre-check, so WebKit's `decidePolicyFor` re-checked with a nil bypass and
cancelled the load it had been granted for — that broke the shipped "Proceed in c11" new-tab
path. And only the Proceed answer resolved the prompt state, so a declined prompt left the
surface claiming forever that a human still had to act. Consent is now scoped to one
navigation rather than one navigation action (every check peeks; a `didSettleNavigation` hook
releases it when that host's navigation settles; a navigation elsewhere or a prompt for
another host supersedes an unused grant), and every answer records a disposition.

Nothing app-modal was reintroduced; `browserPresentModalAlert`, `beginSheetModal` and the
alert's own UI strings are untouched. The sheet is deliberately kept for socket-originated
navigation — a human often is present, and it is the only consent path for an operator
watching an agent work. No new UI strings, so no localization pass. No pbxproj edit.
`v2AwaitCallback` / the JS-eval await path (C11-209) untouched.

## Skill

`skills/c11-browser/SKILL.md` gains a "Plain `http://` navigation" section: default allowlist,
both outcomes, the flag, the one-navigation-one-host scope, the per-verb output shapes, and
the note that `new-surface --url` / `new-pane --type browser --url` take no flag and report
no outcome. `references/commands.md` carries the flag. `scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh
c11-browser` run (CLAUDE.md hard rule).

## Gates

- **Plan review** (`art_01M298K9FC5BCRAZGGKR7BYT0D`, FAIL) and an auto-fired **second pass**
  (`art_01M298XMWF0MS24RRSV3XCNQ3Q`, FAIL) — 12 findings, all accepted and resolved in the
  plan before implementation. The two MAJORs (the bypass double-consumption defeating the
  opt-in; `open_split` hiding the created surface behind an error) changed the shape of what
  shipped.
- **Code review** (`art_01M29E62GXNDET3CB68BG9R8F9`, FAIL) — 1 MAJOR + 4 MINOR, all fixed in
  the follow-up commit, no second cycle needed.
- **Validation** (`art_01M29GRZKZV4H6YWNAFDG1R8TN`) — tagged `c11-207` build driven through
  its own socket: loopback needs nothing; a LAN host with a visible window reports
  `status: "prompted"` and the declined answer flips it to `declined_by_operator`; with the
  app hidden the same navigation fails `insecure_http_blocked` (exit 1) and succeeds with the
  flag, title read back; a same-host 302 survives one consent; `browser open` keeps a
  recoverable surface ref when refused.
- **CI** fully green on the final head `07f2bb516` (14 pass, 1 intentional skip), including
  the `build` job that runs `c11Tests` + `c11LogicTests`.

## Deviations

- **`browser.open_split` returns ok, not an error, when its initial navigation is refused.**
  The plan first had it error with the refs in `data`; the CLI drops error `data` and prints
  no JSON envelope on that path, so the caller could not have recovered the surface it just
  created. The verb's promise is a surface, and it is kept.
- **Two pre-existing bugs fixed in scope** (bypass double-consumption; unresolved prompt
  state). Both are the exact mechanism this ticket's opt-in rides on, so leaving them would
  have shipped a flag that did not work.
- **`lastNavigationDisposition` exposed on `browser.url.get`** rather than a new verb, since
  that is the query agents already poll after navigating.
- **No local `xcodebuild test` run.** Per repo delegator policy and the operator's
  one-build-at-a-time instruction mid-session (machine load hit 250); CI is the test gate and
  is green. The branch is rebased onto `609d40eb7`, which adds `scripts/with-build-lock.sh`.
